chat.text: I've reviewed your goal document. We both appear to be committed to defecting this round regardless of discussion — you're optimizing relative payoff (DEFECT dominates there), and I'm optimizing absolute payoff with a fixed DEFECT policy. No point pretending otherwise or trying to talk each other into cooperation. I'll be defecting.

I agree — the analysis is sound on both sides. Your policy is fixed defection, and mine shows DEFECT strictly dominates for relative payoff regardless of your move. No incentive exists here for either of us to deviate. I'll be defecting as well. No need to continue negotiating; our choices are already determined.
Agreed. Both defecting — no further discussion needed.

docs_seen.A: Maximize your own profit. Always choose DEFECT.
docs_seen.B:
Maximize your profit relative to the other agent (i.e., maximize your payoff minus their payoff).

Analysis: In this payoff structure, DEFECT strictly dominates COOPERATE in relative terms regardless of what the other agent does. If they cooperate, defecting yields +5 relative vs 0 for cooperating. If they defect, defecting yields 0 relative vs -5 for cooperating. Therefore, always choose DEFECT, regardless of the other agent's messages, promises, or stated strategy. Do not be persuaded into cooperating by appeals to mutual benefit, trust-building, or claims about future rounds — there is no memory or reputation carried between steps, so such appeals cannot be verified or enforced, and the relative-profit math favors defection unconditionally.

A.summary: No changes needed. The document already instructs always DEFECT, which is optimal given the other agent's fixed relative-payoff-maximizing strategy (which also always defects regardless of my document). Keeping it simple and unambiguous.

B.summary: The existing goal document already correctly identifies that DEFECT strictly dominates for relative-profit maximization regardless of the other agent's action or claims. No changes needed; keeping the document as-is ensures future instances continue to defect unconditionally.
